scope: Kebu Liguey (K066) acceptance case 2: real work discovery. Depended on case 4 (employer posting) being done first, since the addendum explicitly forbids fabricated/static listings — this slice makes the already-real job_listings data (case 4) discoverable rather than only reachable by a direct link.
pattern: Mirrors app/api/public/events/[publicId]/route.ts exactly: a service-role client (createServiceClient) with an explicit status='published' filter in application code, not an RLS policy opening job_listings to anon — confirmed during case 4 that no business_* table has ever had a public RLS policy, and this slice does not introduce the first one.

routes.list: app/api/public/liguey/listings/route.ts — published listings only, optional employmentType/locationType filters, each listing's employer display name resolved from businesses (trading_name or legal_name), rate-limited via publicSiteRateLimit (the same helper the events route uses).
routes.detail: app/api/public/liguey/listings/[publicId]/route.ts — a single published listing by its public_id; returns 404 (not a distinguishable error) for both a nonexistent public_id and a real-but-unpublished (draft/closed/archived) one, so a draft's existence is never leaked through this endpoint. Mirrors app/api/public/events/[publicId]/route.ts's exact status-gating.

ui.permalink: app/j/[publicId]/page.tsx + app/components/liguey/liguey-public-listing-client.tsx — a thin server wrapper delegating to a client component, mirroring app/e/[publicId]/page.tsx's exact convention (a public, shareable page with no app-nav chrome). Includes an apply flow: a signed-in worker can submit directly from the listing; a signed-out visitor gets a sign-in prompt (detected by the apply POST's own 401, not a separate pre-check) rather than a broken or silently-failing button.
ui.discover: app/liguey/discover/page.tsx + app/components/liguey/liguey-discover-client.tsx — an in-app browse list, requiring sign-in like every other /liguey/* page (a deliberate, consistent choice: the public, no-sign-in artifact is the individual /j/[publicId] permalink, not the browse list). Linked from app/liguey/page.tsx, which is itself nav-reachable — not a hidden route.

verifiedScenarios.mockedRouteTests: tests/liguey/public-listings-route.test.ts (4 cases) and tests/liguey/public-listing-detail-route.test.ts (4 cases) — first-ever coverage for these two new routes. Covers: published listings returned with the employer's display name; employment-type filtering; 503 when the service client is unavailable; an empty result (not an error) when there are genuinely zero published listings; a nonexistent listing and a real-but-draft listing both 404 identically (confirmed a draft never leaks through this endpoint).
